Analyst Sees Revolution Medicines Maintaining Dominant Position in Pancreatic Cancer Treatment
Young expects Revolution Medicines to maintain a leading position in pancreatic cancer over the near and long term.
The drug’s second-line approval arrived earlier than expected. Its commercial launch is underway, with physicians reporting rapid adoption.
Meanwhile, four pivotal studies are evaluating daraxonrasib and zoldonrasib in earlier treatment settings, including adjuvant therapy.
The company is also testing combinations with PRMT5 inhibitors and other experimental treatments to improve the durability of patient responses.
Growth Beyond Pancreatic Cancer
Young forecasts $9.8 billion in revenue by 2032, below Bloomberg’s consensus estimate of $12.6 billion.
Her projection includes only second- and third-line non-small cell lung cancer treatment and excludes elironrasib.
However, Young remains bullish on the company’s ability to expand its RAS inhibitors into other cancers. She expects that opportunity to become clearer over the next 12 months.
The RASolve 301 trial, which compares daraxonrasib with docetaxel in previously treated lung cancer patients, is expected to deliver results in 2027.
Early data for zoldonrasib and elironrasib in first-line lung cancer treatment are promising, although patient follow-up remains limited.
Colorectal cancer remains the least validated opportunity. Revolution Medicines expects to present additional data and outline its development strategy in the fourth quarter of 2026.
